title: Ireland – World wide web (www) site design services – Tionscadal Forbartha Teicneolaíochta: Open competition for the design, implementation, support of an integrated examination management ecosystem for TEG – Phase 1 535
description: TEG (Teastas Eorpach na Gaeilge, or “European Certificate in Irish”) is a professional language testing service provided by Maynooth University’s Lárionad na Gaeilge (The Centre for Irish Language). We offer standardised Irish language proficiency exams and certification for learners and skilled users of Irish alike who wish to obtain an independent qualification in Irish that is recognised nationally and internationally. TEG is the only independent certification system available for Irish and the only system that is broadly aligned with the Common European Framework of Reference (CEFR), the most widely used international framework for measuring language ability. TEG exams cover levels A1 to C1 of the CEFR, examining four language skills: speaking, listening, reading and writing. Lárionad na Gaeilge is a member of the Association of Language Testers in Europe (ALTE), an association whose members include major European professional language testing organisations. ALTE monitors and regularly audits TEG examinations to ensure that they meet the highest standards and international best practice. TEG has been awarded the ALTE Q-mark three times, in 2015, 2020 and again in 2025 as confirmation that our exams meet all the core requirements of ALTE's 18 quality standards. TEG has now been in existence for over 20 years and over 23,000 candidates have taken the exams during that time.

title: Finland – Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services – Vesiväylien mittausten turvallisuuskoordinaattori
description: Väylävirasto teettää vesiväylien mittauksia pääasiassa monikeilaamalla ja tankoharaamalla erillisten toimeksiantojen mukaisesti niin Suomen rannikolla kuin sisävesilläkin. Mittaustoimeksiantoja annetaan n. 20–35 vuosittain. Turvallisuuskoordinaattorin tehtävänä on toimia tehtävistään vastuullisena tilaajan edustajana vastaten ja huolehtien tilaajalle säädetyistä turvallisuusvelvoitteista työturvallisuuslainsäädännön mukaisesti. Tulevan hankinnan perusteella valittu tarjoaja vastaa Väyläviraston vesiväylien mittausten turvallisuuskoordinaattorina toimimisesta. Tilaaja toteaa, että suora kilpailija monikeilamittausten ja tankoharausten puitesopimusten toimittajille ei voi toimia turvallisuuskoordinaattorina eikä täten osallistua tulevaan tarjouskilpailuun.

title: Evaluation Scoping Studies (2 Lots)
description: The Gambling Commission is seeking to appoint one or two suppliers to conduct two separate evaluation scoping studies under two separate lots. Both studies will contribute to the Commission's aims of increasing our capacity to evaluate new requirements and policies, using data and analytics to make gambling regulation more effective and demonstrate how our understanding of our outcomes and our approach to evaluation has improved. The recommendations and outputs from both studies will inform the Commission's future evaluation approaches and contribute to wider policy considerations. Lot 1 is focused on the identification of optimum approaches for evaluating the complex topic of harm reduction approaches, including customer interaction. Lot 2 is focused on exploring how collaborative approaches and co-production can be applied to evaluation in the gambling sector. The opportunity is hosted via the Government Commercial Agency's e-Sourcing Portal, Jaggaer, and is being sourced through the Research and Insights Dynamic Purchasing System (RM6126). Suppliers registered on this DPS can access the opportunity. For further details regarding the Research and Insights DPS, please visit https://www.gca.gov.uk/agreements/RM6126. For further details regarding the DPS registration process, please visit https://supplierregistration.cabinetoffice.gov.uk/dps/RM6126?nav=0 Please note, the DPS is owned by the Government Commercial Agency and not the Gambling Commission. Therefore, please direct any queries regarding the DPS to the GCA Customer Service Team on info@gca.gov.uk or call on 0345 410 2222

title: Supply and Delivery of Hygiene Services and Equipment 0226

title: Waste Collection, Fundy National Park
description: BIDS RECEIVED BY FAX AND EMAIL WILL BE ACCEPTED AS OFFICIAL. PARKS CANADA IS NOT CURRENTLY ACCEPTING BIDS VIA SAP ARIBA, YOU MUST SUBMIT YOUR BID VIA FAX OR EMAIL AS INDICATED IN THE SOLICITATION DOCUMENT. BIDS RECEIVED IN-PERSON OR BY COURIER WILL NOT BE ACCEPTED. The only acceptable email address for responses to the bid solicitation is soumissionsest-bidseast@pc.gc.ca. Bids submitted by email directly to the Contracting Authority or to any email address other than soumissionsest-bidseast@pc.gc.ca will not be accepted. The only acceptable facsimile for responses to bid solicitations is 1-877-558-2349. The maximum email file size that Parks Canada is capable of receiving is 15 megabytes. The Bidder is responsible for any failure attributable to the transmission or receipt of the emailed bid due to file size. The Bidder should be cognisant of the size of the email as a whole, and not only the attachments. Please take into consideration that some attachments, when sent, may be resized during the email transfer. If the email size is too large, the Bidder should send the bid in multiple emails properly labeled with the solicitation number, project name, and indicate how many emails are included (ex. 1 of 2). Emails with links to bid documents will not be accepted. Bid documents must be sent as email attachments. REQUIREMENT Parks Canada Agency (PCA) requires a qualified Contractor to perform all tasks related to the collection, transportation and disposal of solid waste, recyclable materials, and construction debris from Fundy National Park. PERIOD OF CONTRACT The period of the Contract is from 01 April 2027 to 31 March 2030 inclusive. ENQUIRIES All enquiries of a technical and contractual nature are to be submitted to the Contracting Authority. Enquiries regarding this solicitation must be submitted in writing and should be received no later than three (3) calendar days prior to the date set for solicitation closing to allow sufficient time to provide a response. Enquiries received after that time may result in an answer NOT being provided. INFORMATION National Parks Regulations require that all work is to be performed in accordance with the ordinances, laws, rules and regulations set out in the National Park Act. Bidders that consider themselves qualified to provide this Work and intend to submit bids on this project should obtain documents from the Government Electronic Tendering Service through the Government of Canada tendering service at www.canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities. Addenda, when issued, will be available from the Government of Canada tendering service. Bidders that elect to base their bids on documents obtained from other sources do so at their own risk. Late submissions will not be considered. The Crown retains the right to negotiate with suppliers on any procurement. Documents may be submitted in either official language of Canada. Parks Canada has made every effort to provide equivalent documents in both official languages, however, if you find any discrepancies between the English and French documents, please notify the contract officer listed in this opportunity as soon as possible so that we can rectify the situation.

Die Lösung soll umfangreiche medizinische Unterlagen automatisiert analysieren, relevante Informationen extrahieren und strukturieren, Behandlungsverläufe darstellen, Recherchefunktionen bereitstellen sowie bei der Erstellung von Sachverhaltsdarstellungen und Gutachtenentwürfen unterstützen. title: Lakisääteisten henkilökuljetusten ja kiireettömien potilaskuljetusten hankinta Etelä-Pohjanmaan hyvinvointialueen palvelutarpeisiin
description: Lakisääteisten henkilökuljetusten ja kiireettömien potilaskuljetusten hankinta Etelä-Pohjanmaan hyvinvointialueen palvelutarpeisiin Hankintayksikkö pyytää tarjousta Lakisääteisten henkilökuljetusten ja kiireettömien potilaskuljetusten toteutuksesta Etelä-Pohjanmaan hyvinvointialueen palvelutarpeisiin; Hankinnan tarkoituksena on toteuttaa tilaajalle kokonaisvaltainen henkilökuljetusten ohjauspalvelukokonaisuus, jolla hallitaan erilaisia Tilaajan sosiaali- ja terveydenhuollon asiakkaille, työntekijöilleen ja muille sidosryhmilleen (palvelun käyttäjät) järjestämiä henkilökuljetuksia sekä vähäisessä hyvinvointialueen tarpeen mukaisia tavarakuljetuksia silloin, kun ne voidaan toteuttaa henkilökuljetuksiin tarkoitetulla kalustolla. Hankinta jakautuu kahteen ajalliseen ja eri sisältöiseen vaiheeseen; vaihe 1 ja vaihe 2. - Vaiheessa 1 palvelun käyttäjien kuljetukset järjestetään tilaajan kilpailuttamien kuljetuspalveluiden tuottajien (jatkossa autoilijat) ajoneuvoilla ja henkilöstöllä, joita ohjauskeskus ohjaa. Tutustu Liite Palvelukuvaus vaihe 1, joka tarkentaa tätä palvelukuvausta vaiheen 1 osalta. - Vaiheessa 2 palvelun käyttäjien kuljetukset järjestetään ohjauskeskuksen omien tai kilpailuttamien tai alihankkijoiden ajoneuvoilla sekä henkilöstöllä, joita ohjauskeskus ohjaa. Tarjoajan tulee tarjota kokonaisuutta. Osatarjouksia ei hyväksytä. Vaihtoehtoisia tarjouksia ei hyväksytä. Tarjouspyyntöasiakirjat ovat suomen kielellä ja tarjous tulee antaa suomen kielellä. Hankintakokonaisuuden tarkemmat tiedot ja vaatimukset tarjouspyynnössä ja liitteissä, erityisesti Liite Hankinnan kohteen kuvaus ja Liite Vaatimusmäärittely, jossa on ilmoitettu tarjottavien palveluiden vähimmäis- ja laatuvaatimukset. Hankinnassa noudatetaan hankintalakia 1397/2016. Menettelytapana on EU-kynnysarvon ylittävä avoin menettely.,

Illumina and PacBio Sequencing of Human and Mouse DNA and RNA
description: The Mechanistic Studies Division (MSD) of Health Canada’s Environmental Health Research and Science Bureau investigates the pathways by which physical, chemical and microbiological agents can cause adverse health effects. To determine how chemical substances cause DNA damage that can lead to illnesses like cancer or inherited diseases, MSD requires high-throughput genome sequencing services utilizing Illumina and Pacific Biosciences (PacBio) platforms. The primary objective of this contract is to secure long-term high-quality sequencing services for pre-prepared DNA libraries and genomic DNA and/or RNA utilizing Illumina or PacBio Revio platforms for the full duration of projects funded until up to 2030-2031. This requirement encompasses the sequencing of multiple mouse and human error-corrected next-generation sequencing (ecNGS) DNA libraries, genomic DNA and/or RNA samples in direct support of four distinct research projects. These projects are distributed across the Division and funded through three separate programs. Collectively, they employ advanced genomic technologies to support public health protection by identifying environmental mutagens, evaluating occupational hazards, and improving toxicological testing methodologies. Specifically, this work will use ecNGS, whole-genome sequencing (WGS), whole-exome sequencing and/or RNA-sequencing approaches to detect and characterize both spontaneous mutations and mutations induced by chemical and environmental exposures in mouse and human DNA as well as gene expression changes. The resulting data will contribute to a better understanding of mutagenic mechanisms, exposure-related genetic damage, and the development of more sensitive and informative approaches for genetic toxicology and human health risk assessment.

title: Germany – Architectural and related services – Generalsanierung mit Erweiterung Inklusionskindergarten in Lappersdorf. Architektenleistungen der Objektplanung Gebäude und Innenräume, Leistungsphasen 5 bis 8, gem. HOAI Teil 3 Abschnitt 1.
description: Der Markt Lappersdorf plant, den vorhandenen Inklusionskindergarten KGL mit 4 Kindergartengruppen zu sanieren und auf 7 Gruppen zu erweitern. Die Programmfläche beträgt insgesamt ca. 1600 qm. Der bestehende eingeschossige Kindergarten aus dem Baujahr 1970 an der Pielmühler Strasse wurde bereits mehrfach umgebaut und im Jahr 1990 erweitert. Der verputzte Mauerwerksbau hat Satteldächer mit unterschiedlichen Deckungen aus Zinkblech, Ziegel sowie teilweise mit einer PV-Anlage. Der Zustand des Kindergartens entspricht funktional nicht mehr dem Stand der Technik und muss saniert werden. Das Gebäude ist insbesondere energetisch und in Bezug auf Brandschutz sowie die Barrierefreiheit veraltet und muss entsprechend ertüchtigt werden. Für die geplante Generalsanierung und Erweiterung wurden die Leistungsphasen 1 - 3 bereits erbracht. Die Baugenehmigung ist beantragt. Das vorliegende VgV-Vergabeverfahren ist Grundlage für die Vergabe der Architektenleistungen der Ausführungsplanung, Vorbereitung und Mitwirkung bei der Vergabe und Objektüberwachung, also der Leistunsphasen 5 bis 8 gem. HOAI. Da eine Bewerbung des vorbefassten Büros nicht ausgeschlossen werden kann, werden zum Ausgleich des Informationsvorsprungs diverse Informationsunterlagen zur Verfügung gestellt, u.a. Planungsgrundlagen, Entwurfsplanung und Kosten. Für die Entwurfsplanung liegt das Nutzungsrecht am Urheberrecht beim Markt Lappersdorf. Die bestehenden 4 Kindergartengruppen sind während der Bauzeit ausgelagert und werden provisorisch in Containern auf dem naheliegenden Rathausparkplatz untergebracht. Die Auslagerung ist nicht Gegenstand des Auftrags. Die Außenanlagen des bestehenden Kindergartens werden während der Bauphase weiter als Freianlagen zum Spielen genutzt. Gegenstand des Auftrags sind die Architektenleistungen der Objektplanung Gebäude und Innenräume gem. HOAI Teil 3 Abschnitt 1, Leistungsphasen 5 bis 8. Der Auftraggeber rechnet für die Kostengruppen 300 und 400 mit Kosten von ca. 6,2 Mio. Euro einschl. Mehrwertsteuer und ordnet die Maßnahme der Honorarzone III zu. Eine Vergabe der Leistungen in Stufen wird vorbehalten. Aus der stufenweisen Beauftragung können keine zusätzlichen Honoraransprüche geltend gemacht werden. Die Planungen sind unmittelbar nach Auftragsvergabe zu beginnen. Voraussichtlich werden folgende Förderprogramme in Anspruch genommen: FAG-Förderung und KfW-Förderung. Betreiber des Kindergartens ist die Katholische Jugendfürsorge der Diözese Regensburg e.V.

title: CAWT PEACEPLUS EASY Project: Early Intervention Support for Children, Young People and Families presenting with Neurodevelopmental Needs (SHSCT Area)
description: This is a project supported by PEACEPLUS, a programme managed by the Special EU Programmes Body (SEUPB). The CAWT PEACEPLUS Early Intervention Support Youth Hubs (EASY) project aims to establish new cross border early intervention support services for families with children and young people presenting with traits consistent with a neurodevelopmental type need or who have been recently diagnosed with a neurodevelopmental condition. By providing help based on presenting need/symptoms, the project aims to improve outcomes for children, young people and their families by helping families' access appropriate support, based on needs at the right time and in the right place. This procurement exercise and the subsequent service to be commissioned will cover only the Northern Ireland delivery area, which is located within the boundaries of the Southern Health and Social Care Trust (SHSCT). Please refer to the full suite of tender documents for further information on the service requirements. This tender has been published on the etendersni.gov.uk (https://etendersni.gov.uk) and all tender documentation is available at the following link: https://etendersni.gov.uk/epps/cft/prepareViewCfTWS.do?resourceId=6534265

title: Water Treatment Chemicals, Testing, Monitoring, and Reporting- Sources Sought Notice / Request for Information
description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE Water Treatment Chemicals, Testing, Monitoring, and Reporting BPA Federal Bureau of Prisons (FBOP) Notice Type Sources Sought / Request for Information / Market Research Agency Federal Bureau of Prisons (FBOP) Contracting Office Federal Bureau of Prisons, Facilities Management Branch 320 First Street NW Washington, DC 20534 Purpose This is a Sources Sought Notice issued solely for market research purposes in accordance with FAR Part 10. The Federal Bureau of Prisons (BOP) is seeking qualified contractors capable of providing water treatment chemicals, water testing, treatment recommendations, reporting, and related support services for federal correctional institutions nationwide, under a Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA). This notice is not a solicitation and does not constitute a commitment by the Government to award a contract or BPA. No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with responding to this notice. The contractor shall furnish all personnel, chemicals, testing equipment, laboratory services, transportation, reporting systems, technical support, and related resources necessary to support boiler water systems, chiller water loops, cooling towers, and domestic water systems at participating BOP facilities. Services include water sampling and analysis, chemical treatment programs, Legionella testing, domestic water testing, water quality reporting, corrective action recommendations, trend analysis, regulatory compliance support, and maintenance of a secure online reporting portal. Contractors shall provide monthly and quarterly reports and maintain water quality treatment programs designed to reduce corrosion, scaling, biological growth, and other operational risks associated with institutional water systems. The requirement includes support for multiple BOP institutions located throughout the United States. Contractors should carefully consider the geographic distribution of performance locations and demonstrate their ability to provide timely service, technical support, testing, and delivery of treatment chemicals to institutions nationwide. Respondents shall identify any planned subcontracting arrangements and provide examples of water treatment, water testing, boiler treatment, cooling tower treatment, Legionella monitoring, or similar services performed directly by their organization as the prime contractor. Experience performed solely by subcontractors or teaming partners should be separately identified. Any future small business set-aside acquisition resulting from this requirement will be subject to the applicable limitations on subcontracting requirements contained in FAR 52.219-14 and 13 CFR �125.6. Respondents should describe how they would comply with these requirements if awarded a contract. Vendors should carefully review the draft requirements before submitting a response. The Government is seeking capability information from firms that can directly perform and support the full scope of services, including water testing, chemical treatment, reporting, and compliance support across multiple correctional institutions. Responses that do not address the firm's ability to meet the requirements outlined herein may be considered less useful for market research purposes. Background The Federal Bureau of Prisons seeks a contractor capable of providing comprehensive water treatment services and chemical products for institutions operating: Steam boiler systems Hot water boiler systems Chilled water systems Cooling towers Domestic water systems The contractor would be responsible for supporting institutions nationwide through testing, treatment recommendations, chemical supply, reporting, and compliance monitoring. Information contained within the draft Statement of Work serves as the basis for this market research effort. Scope of Requirements The Government is interested in determining industry capability to provide the following services: 1. title: Denison Valve Replacement

The work will be performed in a confined space within a manhole approximately 30 feet deep, requiring specialized access, lifting equipment, and appropriate safety measures. The type of set-aside decision to be issued will depend upon the capabilities of the responses to this synopsis.

description: Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC) is asking interested parties to provide information for a potential lease of space that meets the following criteria: Section A: Lease Components • a lease term of approximately 10 years, commencing on or about May 1, 2030, with a right of early termination anytime on or after May 1, 2038 provided written notice is given at least 12 months prior, plus an option to extend the lease for One (1) additional period of Two (2) years; • approximately 4,281 usable square metres (um2) of office space, and one (1) parking space; • the proposed space must be available approximately 65 weeks prior to the above-noted lease commencement date so all space(s) may be prepared for occupancy; • the proposed space should satisfy or be capable of satisfying the following criteria: 1. the proposed space should be within an office or commercial building; industrial type buildings and those with industrial space will not be considered. A mixed use building may be considered at the sole discretion of PSPC; 2. preference may be given to spaces with any or all of the following: a highly visible storefront space, on a main road, with direct pedestrian access from the street; 3. a minimum of 771 um2 of the proposed space must be located on a floor with public access; preference may be given to spaces located on the main floor; 4. the proposed space must be contiguous within each floor; 5. if the proposed space is offered on multiple floors, consecutive floors are preferred; 6. a dedicated telecommunication room measuring no less than 20.3 um² within the proposed space must be provided; this area will not form part of the Lessee’s usable area noted above but will be included in the rentable area calculation; 7. cleaning services will be required during business hours; 8. the proposed space must be fully accessible to persons with a disability; 9. parking for approximately 25 vehicles must be available to the public within a one (1) block radius of the proposed space; 10. a public transit stop must be within 600 metres of the buildings main entrance, and the frequency of service must not be greater than 30 minute intervals between the hours of 0700 hours and 1800 hours, Monday to Friday inclusive and there must be an accessible walking route between the public transit stop and the building; 11. acceptable space for the installation of bicycle rack(s); 12. the physical characteristics of the lands and the building and the area and environment surrounding it, including neighbouring land uses, shall be compatible with the Lessee’s intended use of the accommodation; 13. the dimensions of the proposed space must be compatible for efficient design and use; • the proposed space must be located in the city of Edmonton and within the following boundaries (the geographical boundaries include sites on either side of the roads): North: Whitemud Drive NW to 91 Street NW / 91 Street NW to Roper Road NW / Roper Road NW to 34 Street NW East: 34th Street NW South: Ellerslie Road SW West: 170th Street SW / Terwillegar Drive NW In the event of any discrepancy between the attached map and text description of the geographic boundaries, the text description shall prevail. This map is to be used for presentation purposes only and is not a legal document • on or before the lease commencement date, the proposed space will have to comply with all requirements contained in PSPC’s Standards for Leased Accommodation, a copy of which may be obtained from the contact listed in Section F; Note: PSPC may wish to visit or inspect the proposed space upon reasonable notice and a threat and risk assessment may be undertaken in order to assess potential threats to the security of the proposed space and to the public.

The Federal Bureau of Prisons (FBOP) anticipates issuance of solicitation 15BBNF26Q31000001 for the award of a firm-fixed-price construction contract for a project titled Replace Elevators at the Federal Detention Center (FDC) Miami. FDC Miami is a federal correctional facility located at 33 NE 4th St., Miami, FL 33132. The work to be performed in association with this project includes the following scope: The contractor shall provide all labor, materials and equipment for the Replace Elevators project at FDC Miami. The project includes, but is not limited to, providing all necessary equipment, labor, materials and incidentals to replace four traction and six hydraulic elevators. The Statement of Work included with the solicitation will provide complete requirements for the project. Any secure/locked documents uploaded with the solicitation will require an active vendor registration at https://SAM.gov as well as your Marketing Partner Identification Number (MPIN) associated with your SAM registration. If you encounter problems accessing these documents, please contact the Federal Service Desk at 866-606-8220. The estimated magnitude of the project lies between $5,000,000 - $10,000,000. The magnitude provided is not meant to imply that the project has necessarily been estimated/budgeted to the maximum of the selected range. It merely conveys that the estimate/budget lies somewhere within that range). The North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code applicable to this requirement is 238290 with a corresponding small business size standard of $22.0 million. The solicitation will be available approximately October 14, 2026. The solicitation will be distributed solely through the website at www.sam.gov. Hard copies of the solicitation will not be made available. The website provides download instructions. All future information about this solicitation, including any amendments, will also be distributed solely through this website. Interested parties are responsible for continuously monitoring this website to ensure that they have the most recent information about this proposed contract action. IMPORTANT: Any contractor interested in obtaining a contract award with the Federal Bureau of Prisons must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) at www.sam.gov. This is a total small business set-aside. In order to qualify for award, your business size metrics information entered in your SAM registration must be less than or equal to the size standard specified above (see provision 52.219-1 in the Representations & Certifications section of your registration and view the table therein listing NAICS codes and your indicated business size relative to the assigned NAICS code above). Each bidder's SAM registration will be reviewed by the Government to confirm that your business size meets the small business size standard requirement. All bidders are urged to double check their SAM registration and update as necessary, including the size metrics information. This synopsis is intended only for those who would be entering into a Prime contract with the FBOP for the entirety of this project. The FBOP does not award subcontracts. Subcontracts (if applicable/necessary) are the responsibility of the Prime contractor. The FBOP has no privity of the contract with subcontractors. If you have questions about SAM.gov, Government procurements in general, or need assistance in the preparation of your bid/proposal/offer, a local Procurement Technical Assistance Center (PTAC) may be able to help. The Procurement Technical Assistance Program was authorized by Congress in 1985 in an effort to expand the number of businesses capable of participating in the Government marketplace. To locate a PTAC near you, go to http://www.aptac-us.org.

title: Jacksonville Harbor Maintenance Dredging
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Enterprise Dredge Delivery Center (EDDC) requires a contract to provide maintenance dredging for Jacksonville Harbor. Jacksonville Harbor: The Jacksonville Harbor, FL - FY27 O and M Contract (non-fed sponsor Jacksonville Port Authority (JAXPORT)) for maintenance dredging typically requires hopper and pipeline/mechanical dredge(s) depending on work location in the~ 20-mile federal channel. The dredge(s) must have the capability to dredge maintenance material up to a depth of -47 ft MLLW (w/additional depths for required advanced maintenance areas and allowable over depths) and to transport the dredged sediment to both a designated Dredged Material Placement Area (DMPA) known as Bartram Island and the Ocean Dredge Material Disposal Site (ODMDS) located approximately 6 nautical miles offshore. Dredged material shall be placed upland in Bartram Island Cell F and the Jacksonville ODMDS Release Zone C1 depending on the specific reach to be dredged. The transport distance to the designated placement areas varies significantly, ranging from direct, local placement to a few miles for the upland placement area and up to 6 miles for ocean disposal from the tip of the south jetty. The work is divided into a base and five options. The Contractor shall be required to (a) commence work under this contract within ten (10) calendar days after the date the Contractor receives the notice to proceed, (b) prosecute the work diligently, and (c) complete the entire work ready for use not later than 220 days after the Contractor receives the notice to proceed. The time stated for completion shall include final cleanup of the premises. Base: 120 calendar days. Option A: 15 calendar days. Option B: 20 calendar days. Option C: 30 calendar days. Option D: 25 calendar days. Option E: 10 calendar days. Complete all work within Cut-17 Sta. 0+00 through Cut-41 Sta. 20+00 (BASE work), which are located within an Outstanding Florida Waters (OFW), no later than May 20, 2027.This solicitation is unrestricted. title: Construction Services for Confined Aquatic Disposal Cell Construction and Maintenance Dredging of the Providence River Federal Navigation Project, Providence, Rhode Island.
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, New England District is issuing a Sources Sought Announcement for the upcoming dredging project located in Providence, Rhode Island. This announcement is to determine the interest, availability and capability of Small and Large Business concerns as described below. The NAICS code for this procurement is 237990. The solicitation for this project is anticipated to be issued on or about 15 March 2027. The construction will begin in September 2027 and is expected to take approximately 2 years to complete. The estimated construction cost is between $80,000,000 and $100,000,000. The Providence River Maintenance Dredging project involves two major sequences of dredging and disposal activities. The first work sequence will be the construction of a new Confined Aquatic Disposal (CAD) cell adjacent to the Providence River. The second work sequence under this contract will include maintenance dredging of the Providence River and Harbor Federal Navigation Project (FNP) to its authorized depths and dimensions. The proposed work consists of mechanically dredging approximately 5,500,000 cubic yards (cy) of material using closed clamshell buckets for both major sequences of work over the course of two years. The new CAD cell will be in the Edgewood Basin area located adjacent to the Providence FNP (hereafter the �Edgewood Shoals North (ESN) CAD cell�). To access the CAD cell area, an access channel will be dug between the Providence FNP and the CAD cell area. The access channel will be approximately 100 ft wide and -25 MLLW deep. The CAD cell will have surface dimensions of approximately 1000 ft. by 1000 ft. and be dug to a depth of -60 MLLW. The material excavated to build the access channel is generally a mix of sandy silt and shell fragments. Within the CAD cell area the material is generally described as soft grey to black organic silt with some layers of firm sandy silt and some shell fragments and coarse-grained material. Material excavated from the access channel and CAD cell area will be placed at four locations: Port Edgewood Basin, the Fox Point Reach CAD cells, Prudence Island Disposal Site, and the Rhode Island Sound Disposal Site. This work consists of mechanically dredging approximately 3,200,000 cy to construct thew ESN CAD cell and its access channel, which must be completed before maintenance dredging of the FNP can begin. The maintenance dredging proposed work consists of mechanically dredging the Providence River FNP to the full -40 MLLW depth plus 2-feet of allowable overdepth. 2,300,000 cy (1,200,000 cy required depth, with up to 1,100,000 cy overdepth) of shoaled material consisting generally of poorly graded medium to fine sand with silt. The dredge material from this maintenance portion of work will be placed in the ESN CAD cell. Environmental coordination and permitting is being completed by the U.S. Army of Engineers, New England District. All dredging and disposal activities for this project have prescribed work windows that incorporate environmental and recreational time of year restrictions. Refer to the Draft Specification Section provided with this announcement for specifics on the time of year work restrictions. In order to accomplish all dredging requirements within the specified dredging window it is expected that the Contractor will need to meet a production rate of 300,000 CY per 30 calendar days. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, New England District is requesting responses to the questions below from both small and large businesses[MC1] . Draft drawings showing a concept design plan and draft Specification Section of 01 11 00 SUMMARY OF WORK have been provided with this announcement to help provide more context for the contract work and responses to these questions. Considering the different disposal locations, are there suggestions on a bid structure that will provide for the most accurate costs of different disposal locations? Any draft restrictions that may impact dredging and/or disposal operations? Any concerns on the period of performance of September 2027 to September 2029 considering the environmental windows and amount of work? If so, why? Any comments about the bed leveling planned in the Fox Point Reach? Are there concerns about this part of the plan, if so, why? Interested firms should also demonstrate their project experience, by providing two (2) projects within the last ten years, which meet the following requirements: Dredging by mechanical means demonstrating a minimum production rate of 300,000 cubic yards in one consecutive 30-day period. Experience with placement of dredged material at an open water placement site in New England during the fall/winter months of October through March. Interested firms should submit a capabilities package to include the following: business classification (i.e. HUBZone, etc.), type of equipment the firm is proposing to use on the project, and two (2) example projects performed by the firm in the last ten (10) years (including Points of Contact for those projects) showing experience with the proposed equipment at the production rate listed above. Please indicate the team subcontractor(s) (if any), including their prior experience and qualifications meeting the same qualifications listed above, which will be used to support the bidder's effort. Firms may use subcontractor experience to demonstrate experience with the requirements, but the role and work performed by each team member (prime and subcontractors) on projects demonstrating that team member's experience shall be the same as the role for that team member for this project. Bid bond will need to be provided with the bid. Responses are limited to twenty pages and due by December 03 , 2026. Responses should be addressed to the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, New England District, 696 Virginia Road, Concord, MA 01742-2751, ATTN: Kyle Hall, or electronically to Kyle.K.Hall@usace.army.mil. The Government will not pay for any material provided in response to this market survey nor return the data provided. This notice is for information purposes only and is not a request to be placed on a solicitation mailing list nor is it a Request for Proposal (RFP) or an announcement of a solicitation. The results of this survey will be considered to be in effect for a period of one year from the date of this notice. title: PIGA Float Assembly Repair Program
description: Login at https://piee.eb.mil and search for 'FA821426RB002' to obtain more details.* Documents related to this procurment are only available through PIEE. 1. Executive Summary: Background & Objective The U.S. Air Force has a critical requirement to support the Minuteman III (MMIII) Intercontinental Ballistic Missile (ICBM) by maintaining the operational readiness of the Missile Guidance Set (MGS) to meet warfighter requirements. Specifically, this effort supports the repair line for the Pendulous Integrated Gyroscopic Accelerometer (PIGA) Float Assembly. The PIGA Float is a critical and precise sub-assembly that serves as the heart of the PIGA instrument, enabling it to measure missile acceleration. Each MGS contains three separate PIGA instruments (each housing a PIGA Float). Without this critical component, the ICBM would cease to function properly. The PIGA Float repair effort is a continuous operation necessary to avoid mission degradation. Quality control and precision engineering are paramount due to the strategic importance of the MMIII weapon system. The contractor must maintain stringent quality assurance protocols to guarantee that each repaired PIGA Float meets the rigorous military specifications. 2. Scope of Work The contractor shall provide the necessary personnel, facilities, and expertise to support the PIGA Float Assembly repair line. The primary scope includes: Repair Operations - The re-manufacture, rebuild, and repair of PIGA Float Assemblies. Volume / Throughput - The repair of 96 PIGA Floats per year. Government Furnished Equipment (GFE) - The repair and/or replacement of GFE as required to support continuous operation of the PIGA Float repair line 3. Contract Structure & Period of Performance The Government anticipates awarding an Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract utilizing a mix of Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee (CPFF) and Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) pricing arrangements. Contract Duration - 5-Year IDIQ Anticipated Ordering Period - 1 November 2026 � 31 October 2031 Task Order Structure - Annual issuance of new, two-year non-severable Task Orders 4. Acquisition Authority & Strategy In accordance with Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Subpart 5.1, this solicitation is an intended sole-source procurement. The Government will solicit and negotiate with only one source: Honeywell Aerospace (CAGE: 09128). This action is taken under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), as implemented by RFO 6.103-1. Market research�including Sources Sought Synopsis FA821425CBPIGA (posted 29 May 2025)�concluded that Honeywell Aerospace is the only responsible source capable of fulfilling the Government�s requirement without causing unacceptable delays to the MMIII weapon system mission. Note: While this is not a request for competitive proposals, information received from other responsible sources identifying their interest and capability will be considered solely to determine whether to conduct a competitive procurement in the future, at the Government�s discretion. 5. Proposal Submission Instructions All proposals submitted in response to this solicitation must be submitted electronically through the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) Solicitation Module. No other methods of proposal submission (e.g., email, hard copy, DoD SAFE) will be accepted. Offerors must be registered in PIEE and have the appropriate roles activated to submit proposals via the Solicitation module prior to the proposal due date. Cost & Pricing Data: The Government requests that ProPricer models (version v9.5.105.2) be submitted in conjunction with all Certified Cost and Pricing Data. Mandatory Pricing Rubric: Submission of the attached Pricing Rubric is a mandatory requirement. Proposals submitted without a completed Pricing Rubric will be automatically rejected by the PIEE solicitation module and will not be considered for evaluation. Submission Cutoff: Proposals will not be accepted after the solicitation closes. Timely submission is the sole responsibility of the offeror, and late proposals will not be evaluated unless otherwise stated under RFO guidelines.

This opportunity is only available to Small Businesses. The U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service Great American Outdoors Act (GAOA) Construction Team has a requirement for the following: Construction services are needed to install a new water main extension that will be connected to an existing water distribution system. The work will include pipe, water main connection, water meter and vault, air/vacuum release valves, gate valve and box, horizontal drilling, and underground utility crossing at the White Horse Hill National Game Preserve in St. Michael, ND in Benson County. This requirement is being procured in accordance with FAR Part 15, Contracting by Negotiation. This will be a Firm Fixed Priced Contract and Award will be based on Lowest Price Technically Acceptable. The complete Solicitation will be posted to https://sam.gov/ under Contract Opportunities on or about November 3, 2026. Interested contractors must be registered in SAM (System for Award Management, www.sam.gov) and complete Online Representations and Certifications. The work will commence within 10 days of Notice to Proceed and be completed by the agreed upon date at the time of award. title: DESIGN-BID-BUILD (DBB) PHASE III GROUNDWATER TREATMENT PLANT CONSTRUCTION, NWIRP BETHPAGE, WANTAGH, NEW YORK
description: Solicitation Number: N4008527R0048 This notice does NOT constitute a request for proposal, request for quote, or invitation for bid. The intent of this pre-solicitation synopsis is to make notice of a proposed contract action for performing construction services for Design-Bid-Build (DBB) Phase III Groundwater Treatment Plant Construction, Naval Weapons Industrial Reserve Plant (NWIRP) Bethpage, Wantagh, New York. PROJECT DESCRIPTION: This Design-Bid-Build project aims to address a plume of contaminated groundwater that has spread south from the former NWIRP and Northrop Grumman properties. This contamination, primarily consisting of chlorinated VOCs (like TCE) and 1,4-dioxane, is being remediated as required by the Navy and the New York State Department of Environmental Conservation. The core of this phase is the construction of a new Groundwater Treatment Plant (GWTP) designed to intercept the leading edge of the plume. The plant will treat the captured water to meet drinking water standards using a process that includes sand filters, an Advanced Oxidation Process (AOP), and Granular Activated Carbon (GAC). The scope of work involves the complete construction and commissioning of the facility. This includes completing three groundwater recovery wells and the associated underground piping to bring contaminated water to the plant. The facility itself will house numerous systems, including large storage tanks, multiple filter types, the AOP system, and granular activated carbon units. The project also covers the construction of two new buildings for the treatment plant and offices, along with all necessary structural, electrical, and plumbing infrastructure. The work includes: buried piping systems, pavements, and miscellaneous items; one underground vault; piping, valves, fittings for three recovery wells and wiring, instruments, and equipment within the conduit, manholes, and vaults; three Reinforced Plastic (FRP) vertical storage tanks; one glass fused Backwash waste steel tank; three Multimedia Vertical Pressure Filters (MMF) unit vessels, two Horizontal Cartridge Filters, one Ozone-Hydrogen Peroxide Advance Oxidation Process (AOP) system; three Liquid Phase Granular Activated Carbon (LGAC) unit vessels; eight pumps with piping, valves, supports and appurtenances; two blowers; chemical feed systems for Sodium Hydroxide, Sodium Hypochlorite and Hydrogen Peroxide; two buildings (treatment plant and office), foundations, and interior/exterior concrete slabs on grade and under-slab utility coordination; structural and architectural roof and systems; one 1200A, 277/480V, 3-phase, 3-Wire Service; an MCC for motor VFDs; heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC); a PLC and SCADA system, and internet/cellular gateway to enable off- site Phase III System process parameters; earthwork, including pad excavation and site re-grading; site utilities; fencing; and a fire protection system. The completion time for this contract is 1,095 calendar days after award. This solicitation is being advertised as "Unrestricted" for full and open competition. This source selection procurement requires both non-price (technical and past performance) and price proposals and will utilize the best value continuum process at FAR 15.103-1 (DPCAP CD 2026-O0048, Rev 1), Tradeoff approach. The basis for evaluation and evaluation factors for award will be included in the solicitation. Large business concerns are required to submit a subcontracting plan prior to award of the contract. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code for this project is 237110, Water and Sewer Line and Related Structures Construction, with a small business size standard of $45,000,000. The magnitude of construction for this project is between $25,000,000 and $100,000,000. The anticipated award of this contract is March 2027. title: Sonic Boom Launch Noise Analysis RFI _NAICS 541330, 541715
description: This is a Request for Information (RFI) for market intelligence and for informational purposes only. This announcement does not constitute a solicitation or a request for proposals (RFP), and no solicitation is currently available. Participation in this RFI is strictly voluntary. The Government will not be obligated to award any agreement or contract because of this RFI, nor will it reimburse respondents for any costs associated with the preparation or submission of information. Submitting a response will not affect a firm's ability to submit a proposal should a formal solicitation be issued in the future. Facilities and infrastructure at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station (CCSFS) are exposed to intense acoustic loads and sonic booms from an increasing cadence of launch operations. Existing historical data is primarily based on aircraft overflights and has limited applicability to the unique pressure signatures generated by modern launch vehicles (including Falcon 9, Falcon Heavy, Starship/Super Heavy, Vulcan, New Glenn, and other current or proposed vehicles). The Government requires development of a scientifically defensible material testing methodology and a predictive engineering model to evaluate the effects of launch noise and sonic booms on both current and legacy construction materials, infrastructure, and facility types at CCSFS. The effort shall support informed decisions on facility sustainment, retrofitting, or replacement. Reference the attached Statement of Objective for a more detailed description of this requirement. Please see attached RFI for further directions. Please respond to the questions found within the RFI document if interested no later than 3 December 2026, 2:00 PM EST. You may address questions in a narrative, annotated outline, bullet or table format. Thank you!

description: DESCRIPTION: This is a Pre-Solicitation Notice for project number 596A4-27-101 that requires Architect/Engineering (A/E) Design Services to Upgrade Fire Alarm System at the Lexington VA Healthcare System, Troy Bowling Campus. Project will replace existing fire alarm system at the Troy Bowling Campus to include Building 1, Building 1A and Building 4. Replacement includes hospital space, parking garage as well as crawl space as required per code. Size of existing facility is 537,542 square feet. Existing fire alarm system is required to remain in service until new system is active and ready to be utilized. Phasing of cutover from existing to new system to be determined by A/E. Project will correct FCA Deficiencies 338139, 45058, 49003, 49909, 49035, 49963 and 49935. New fire alarm system will be required to interact with multiple systems throughout the hospital to include, but not limited to: Door magnets, elevators, HVAC systems, kitchen hood systems, sprinkler system, specialty fire suppression systems, door locking systems, smoke dampers, duct detectors and other systems. The estimated magnitude of construction for this A/E requirement is between $10,000,000 and $20,000,000. END OF DESIGN SCOPE SYNOPSIS Digital copies of the as-builts are limited. title: Air Force Contract Augmentation Program (AFCAP) VI
description: The 772nd Enterprise Sourcing Squadron (772 ESS/PKD) is issuing this solicitation for the Air Force Contract Augmentation Program VI (AFCAP VI). This is a Multiple-Award Indefinite-Delivery/Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract designed to provide rapid, global contingency planning, logistics, and emergency construction capabilities to the Department of the Air Force, other DoD components, and Federal agencies. The AFCAP serves as a responsive, global force multiplier for commanders and Government agencies, supporting contingencies both within the contiguous United States (CONUS) and outside the contiguous United States (OCONUS).The AFCAP supports United States (U.S.) national interests and security objectives by providing rapid-response capabilities for contingency planning, deployment, training/equipping of forces, emergency/contingency construction, logistics/commodities, and services. These capabilities align with definitions in the DOD Dictionary of Military and Associated Terms. AFCAP provides a full range of Base Operating/Life Support (BOS/BLS) and logistical support on an as-required basis to support a wide spectrum of activities, including, but are not limited to: Major Theater War(s); Small Scale Contingencies; Irregular Warfare; responses to Violent Extremist Organizations (VEO); foreign assistance, developmental assistance, humanitarian assistance, and security assistance (including Foreign Military Sales); peacekeeping; counterinsurgency, counterdrug and counterterrorism operations; maritime security operations; recovery operations and denial measures; domestic/international emergency support; infrastructure/facility design/build, design/build/operate, demolition, and site restoration; deliberate and crisis action planning; and military exercises (including Joint Chiefs of Staff sponsored) authorized by the National Command Authority.

description: **ONLY SEAPORT MAC HOLDERS ARE ELIGIBLE FOR AWARD UNDER THIS SOLICITATION.*** Request for Proposal (RFP) (N6133127R0006) under the Seaport NxG Multiple Award Contract (MAC), for Mission Module Engineering and Technical Support. This effort has been previously been posted under the Opportunities page as the following: Sources Sought Notice (N6133126SNQ27), dated (Posted 7 May 2026) and the follow-up Advance Planning Notice/Pre-Solicitation Notice dated (16 June 2026). ***RESPONSES MUST BE SUBMITTED VIA THE PIEE SOLICITATION MODULE.*** ***ALL DOCUMENTS ARE AVAILABLE WITHIN THE PIEE SOLICITATION MODULE*** Questions and Answers WILL TAKE PLACE THROUGH PIEE MODULE AND POSTED TO PIEE SOLICITATION MODULE BY ATTACHMENT***This is a solicitation for SEAPORT MAC HOLDERS ONLY. This solicitation is to provide services to support the Naval Surface Warfare Center Panama City Division (NSWC PCD) Modular Integration Division as the lead for engineering, analysis, and planning support for the modularization of off-board systems in support of the littoral warfare mission area. The requirements will include systems engineering, packaging and handling of off-board system hardware, system integration of legacy and emerging littoral mission systems, sea frame integration of mission modules, development of mission system common computing environments (e.g. Mission Package Computing Environment (MPCE)) and integrated communications networks (e.g. Multiple Vehicle Communication System(MVCS)), distributed engineering testing, and supporting the Government in validation and verification. Specifically, these requirements include the general program, engineering, technical, and integrated logistics support requirements for the Littoral Combat Ship (LCS)Mission Modules (MM) program at NSWC PCD. title: Hydropower Technical Research & Knowledge Exchange
description: 1. General. This is a SOURCES SOUGHT for an upcoming Service Contract for HYDROPOWER TECHNICAL RESEARCH AND KNOWLEDGE EXCHANGE. It is for informational/market research purposes only. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL, QUOTATION OR BID, NOR A SYNOPSIS OF A PROPOSED CONTRACT ACTION UNDER FAR SUBPART 5.2. This Sources Sought is to gain knowledge of the interest, capabilities, and qualifications of industry so the government can make informed business decisions. We are seeking responses from both large and small business members of industry to include: Small Business, Small Disadvantaged Businesses to include 8(a) firms, Historically Underutilized Business Zones (HUBZone), Woman-Owned Small Business (WOSB) to include Economically Disadvantaged Women-Owned Small Business (EDWOSB), Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small business (SDVOSB) and Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB). All interested parties are highly encouraged to respond. Reponses to this Sources Sought announcement will be used by the Government to make business decisions and to inform potential future solicitations. a. The North American Industrial Classification Code (NAICS) for this requirement is: 541990 - All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services b. The related size standard is: $19.5M c. Product Service Code is: R425 d. Formal Sources Sought Response Due � December 3, 2026 at 12:00pm Pacific Time. 2. Background. As the nation's leading hydropower asset owner and operator with 75 Corps owned hydropower projects across the U.S., USACE is charged with improving the capability, reliability, and safety of the Corps' hydropower infrastructure by developing or advancing state-of-the-art technology, innovative practices, and operational improvements. USACE's Hydroelectric Design Center (HDC) located in Portland, OR, Engineering Research and Development Center (ERDC) located in Vicksburg, MS, and the Hydropower R&D Advisory Committee (members from HDC, ERDC, HQ, and the Corps' 16 hydropower Districts) have taken the lead on managing the Hydropower R&D mission to include determining the industry needs, setting priorities, and managing the execution. 3. Project Scope. a. USACE Hydropower is conducting market research to identify available approaches for obtaining relevant technical information and research findings, exchanging technical knowledge with other owners and operators, and addressing shared technical problems. The government seeks access to technical research, practical guidance, and industry operating experience to support decisions concerning the design, operation, maintenance, protection, and modernization of hydropower facilities and associated electrical infrastructure. The anticipated areas of interest are: Hydropower equipment design, operation, maintenance, and associated best practices. Protection and control systems for hydropower facilities and associated electrical infrastructure. Economic evaluation and modeling of hydropower assets to support modernization planning. Potential approaches may include access to existing technical publications, technical exchanges, research services, collaborative investigations, training, or combinations of these services both virtually and through conference/workshop forums. b. Anticipated Period of Performance: January 01, 2027 � December 31, 2027 c. Number and Type of Contracts: NWP contemplates awarding one firm fixed price service contract. 4. Submission Instructions. Formal responses to this Sources Sought notice must be submitted electronically (via email) with SUBJECT: Sources Sought � Hydropower Technical Research. Please email to Nicholas Weaver, Contract Specialist, at Nicholas.E.Weaver@usace.army.mil and Contracting Officer, at nicole.a.adams@usace.army.mil before 12:00PM Pacific Time on December 03, 2026. Interested parties� responses to this Sources Sought shall be limited to six (6) pages and shall include the following information: Firm's name, address, point of contact, phone number, e-mail address, CAGE and Unique Entity ID Firm's business category and size: Large Business (include summary of small business participation metrics), Small Business, Small Disadvantaged Businesses to include 8(a) firms, Historically Underutilized Business Zones (HUBZone), Woman-Owned Small Business (WOSB) to include Economically Disadvantaged Women-Owned Small Business (EDWOSB), Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small business (SDVOSB) and at the subcontracting level, Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB). An explanation of the prime firm�s capabilities, special qualifications/certifications and equipment and describe the work to be self-performed as it pertains to the proposed work outlined in the Project Scope. In submitting capability statements for consideration, offers should address the following: i. Which capabilities you provide, how they are delivered, and any limitations on access or use. ii. Which of the three technical subject areas they support. iii. Describe available research, publications, technical exchanges, training, and research-participation opportunities. iv. Provide representative topics or examples sufficient to demonstrate relevance. v. Explain access arrangements, licensing restrictions, and internal-sharing limitations. vi. Distinguish services included in a standard offering from separately priced services. 4. Project Examples (for Joint Ventures, please include projects completed by the Joint Venture if available): i. To be considered for a potential set aside strategy, provide a maximum of three (3), minimum of one (1) project(s). These project examples must be similar in size, scope and complexity to the work described in paragraph 3 of this notice, with a description of each project (to include pertinent qualitative and quantitative information about featured scope elements), and include the following: Project Title Contract Number Contract award date Customer name, phone number and email address Prime or Subcontractor Initial contract dollar value Final contract dollar value Initial contract completion date Final contract completion date Customer satisfaction Note: The Government may verify information in CPARS or PPIRS. 5. Firm's Joint Venture information if applicable - existing and potential. 6. Firm's interest and the likelihood in bidding on the solicitation when it is issued. (Refer to planned advertise and performance dates) 5. Disclaimer and Important Notes. This notice does not obligate the Government to award a contract. No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this Sources Sought or any follow up information. The Government reserves the right to use information provided by respondents for any purpose deemed necessary and legally appropriate. Any organization responding to this notice should ensure that its response is complete and sufficiently detailed to allow the Government to determine the organization's capabilities to perform the work. Respondents are advised that the Government is under no obligation to acknowledge receipt of the information received or to provide feedback to respondents with respect to any information submitted. All interested firms must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) at https://www.sam.gov to have size status considered. You must remain current for the duration of the source selection process to be eligible for award of a Government contract.

title: LOWER BRULE NORTH SHORELINE STABILIZATION AND ECOSYSTEM RESTORATION, ELEMENT 2
description: The project is located along the left descending bank of Lake Sharpe near the Lower Brule, SD town site. Lower Brule North Element 2 includes a 100-foot-wide riparian planting bench, a gravel maintenance path along the entire reach, a riprap revetment to protect the shoreline and island from erosion, and the creation of a 200-by-1,500-foot island constructed in water up to three feet deep. The sheltered open water area between the island and the shoreline will develop into approximately 5.17 acres of emergent wetland, and this will also create approximately 32 acres of riparian habitat. Related tasks include earth moving, grading, bank shaping, rock installation, water management, fill, and topsoil placement.

title: Air Force Contract Augmentation Program (AFCAP) VI
description: The 772nd Enterprise Sourcing Squadron (772 ESS/PKD) is issuing this solicitation for the Air Force Contract Augmentation Program VI (AFCAP VI). This is a Multiple-Award Indefinite-Delivery/Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract designed to provide rapid, global contingency planning, logistics, and emergency construction capabilities to the Department of the Air Force, other DoD components, and Federal agencies. The AFCAP serves as a responsive, global force multiplier for commanders and Government agencies, supporting contingencies both within the contiguous United States (CONUS) and outside the contiguous United States (OCONUS).The AFCAP supports United States (U.S.) national interests and security objectives by providing rapid-response capabilities for contingency planning, deployment, training/equipping of forces, emergency/contingency construction, logistics/commodities, and services. These capabilities align with definitions in the DOD Dictionary of Military and Associated Terms. AFCAP provides a full range of Base Operating/Life Support (BOS/BLS) and logistical support on an as-required basis to support a wide spectrum of activities, including, but are not limited to: Major Theater War(s); Small Scale Contingencies; Irregular Warfare; responses to Violent Extremist Organizations (VEO); foreign assistance, developmental assistance, humanitarian assistance, and security assistance (including Foreign Military Sales); peacekeeping; counterinsurgency, counterdrug and counterterrorism operations; maritime security operations; recovery operations and denial measures; domestic/international emergency support; infrastructure/facility design/build, design/build/operate, demolition, and site restoration; deliberate and crisis action planning; and military exercises (including Joint Chiefs of Staff sponsored) authorized by the National Command Authority.

title: Weapons Shipping Harness Refurbishment Blanket Purchase Agreement
description: This is a limited sources combined synopsis/solicitation for services prepared in accordance with simplified acquisition procedures found in the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Revolutionary Far Overhaul (RFO) Subpart 13.2, effective 1 February 2026, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation/notice; further written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation Number N6278927Q0001 is issued as a Request for Quotes (RFQ). The solicitation and incorporated provisions and clauses are in effect through the most current Federal Acquisition Circular (FAC) 2026-01 with an effective date of 13 March 2026. The Product and Service Code (PSC) is J019. The North American Industry Classification (NAICS) code is 336419. Supervisor of Shipbuilding Conversion and Repair, Groton CT (SSGR) intends to enter into a multiple award Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA), for a period of 5 years. The vendor shall refurbish weapon Shipping Harnesses in accordance with the attached specification. The Period of Performance shall be 27 January 2027 to 26 January 2032. Each BPA will have up to a five (5) year ordering period with a ceiling of up to $500,000. The BPA Call Limit will be $100,000. The ceiling of each agreement can be increased or decreased at any time by the Contracting Officer via bilateral modification to meet current and future requirements. Funding is not assigned to the BPA. The Government will only be obligated to the extent of calls placed against an awarded BPA. Each BPA call will be competed among the agreement holders as requirements arise. A call will then be placed based on the quote that is most advantageous to the Government. Offerors must provide a description of their property management system per FAR 45.201(c)(4) or confirmation of a property management system that has been reviewed and approved per DFARS 242.302 and meets the requirements of FAR 52.245-1(f). Offerors shall submit a pricing schedule that covers each year of the Period of Performance as follows: Fiscal Year Service Unit Unit Price Amount 2027 U-SSN 688 Weapon Shipping Harness Refurb 1 JOB $XX.XX $XX.XX 2028 U-SSN 688 Weapon Shipping Harness Refurb 1 JOB $XX.XX $XX.XX 2029 U-SSN 688 Weapon Shipping Harness Refurb 1 JOB $XX.XX $XX.XX 2030 U-SSN 688 Weapon Shipping Harness Refurb 1 JOB $XX.XX $XX.XX 2031 U-SSN 688 Weapon Shipping Harness Refurb 1 JOB $XX.XX $XX.XX Quotations are due prior to 4:00PM EST, 3 December 2026. Late submissions will not be accepted. Offers should be submitted via electronic commerce. The electronic address for receipt of offers is: kyle.r.berg3.civ@us.navy.mil and stephanie.l.neale.civ@us.navy.mil. Offerors should identify the RFQ number in the Subject Line of the email. Offerors are advised to submit electronic documents early and confirm successful transmission/receipt. The System for Award Management (SAM) is a Government maintained database of companies wanting to do business with the Government. A firm must register and maintain an active SAM registration in order to receive a federal award. Register at: https://sam.gov/SAM/pages/public/index.js EVALUATION FACTORS FOR AWARD: The Government intends to enter into a multiple award Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA), for a period of 5 years. Each BPA call will be competed among the agreement holders as requirements arise. The Government will make award(s) to the offeror(s) that represent the best value to the Government based on the following factors, in order: -Technical Qualifications/Ability to meet schedule -Past Performance -Price The Government intends to evaluate proposals and award a contract without discussions with offerors. However, the Government reserves the right to conduct discussions if later determined by the Contracting Officer to be necessary. The Government reserves the right to award one line, all line items, or any combination thereof. If multiple line items are awarded, cost/prices for each line item will be totaled and the award amount will be based on that total. See Section M of the solicitation for additional details.

title: Supplemental F/A-18E/F and EA-18G Service Life Modification (SLM) Capacity Request for Information (RFI)
description: The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR), on behalf of the F/A-18E/F and EA-18G Program Office (PMA-265), is conducting market research to determine the industrial base�s existing capability and facility capacity to provide supplemental or secondary Service Life Modification (SLM) turnkey capacity for F/A-18E/F Super Hornet and EA-18G Growler aircraft starting in FY29. The Government seeks mature, currently operational�facilities, personnel, processes, tooling, and infrastructure capable of supporting SLM workload. The Government is not seeking conceptual or developmental solutions that would require significant new construction, extensive infrastructure development, or multi-year implementation before becoming operational. The Government currently executes these requirements through a hybrid framework utilizing the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) (The Boeing Company) and a Naval Aviation Enterprise organic depot (Fleet Readiness Center Southwest) under a public private partnership with the OEM. To support long-term strike fighter inventory requirements, the Government is evaluating the availability of additional commercial or second-source depot modification repair overhaul (MRO) capacity. Information submitted in response to this notice will assist the Government in determining its long-term acquisition strategy through 2038, including whether to establish an additional qualified source to supplement the current capacity or maintain the current hybrid framework mentioned above under the authority of FAR 6.103-3(b)(1) (Defense Pricing, Contracting, and Acquisition Policy (DPCAP) Class Deviation (CD) 2026-O0017) / 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(3)(A) (Industrial Mobilization). PMA-265 anticipates a maximum SLM induction profile of up to 47 aircraft per year across the industrial base. Actual aircraft allocation among available sources may vary based on Fleet requirements, aircraft availability, demonstrated performance, schedule, and available capacity. 1. Scope of Interest The Government is seeking information on industry capability to perform the SLM workload to supplement current capacity, including but not limited to: Aircraft induction, preservation, inspection, and documentation; F/A-18E/F and EA-18G SLM Specification Modification work; Installation of applicable Structural Technical Directives (TDs) and Advanced Capability Modifications such as Block III upgrade kits; Procurement and management of all required material, including long-lead material, using corporate approaches that support anticipated year-of-execution requirements and ensure material is available for installation when required; Inspection-based repairs and structural modifications; Manufacturing or sourcing of repair parts and materials, as required; Aircraft systems troubleshooting and functional verification; Aircraft records and database updates; and Support for Functional Check Flights and coordination with Government representatives. The Government recognizes that individual respondents may be capable of supporting only a subset of this work or a limited annual quantity. Responses identifying supplemental capability, secondary capability, or potential teaming arrangements are encouraged. 2. Information Requested Interested firms are requested to provide the following information: I. Company Information Company name, address, point of contact, telephone number, and email address. Business size and applicable socioeconomic status, if any. Relevant experience performing MRO / depot-level maintenance, advanced avionic systems modification, modernization, structural repair, or sustainment work on tactical aircraft. II. Facility Information Location(s) of existing facilities proposed for this effort. Number, type, and dimensions of available aircraft bays or work positions, including usable floor area, hangar-door dimensions, overhead clearance, and any facility limitations. For planning purposes, the aircraft footprint is 45 feet wide by 61 feet long Availability of a suitable runway and airfield support for F/A-18 and EA-18G series aircraft. Current facility utilization and the earliest date capacity could be made available. Access to required security, quality assurance, tooling, material handling, and aircraft-support infrastructure. Current, or ability to obtain, Defense Security Services (DSS) facility clearance of Secret. Consistent with Executive Order 14372, Prioritizing the Warfighter in Defense Contracting, and the USW(A&S) memorandum, Prioritizing the Warfighter and Negotiation of Contractor Facilitation Costs (dated 4 May 2026), respondents shall identify whether they anticipate using their own capital to fund stand-up costs necessary to perform the proposed work and describe any Government support, reimbursement, or other enablers required to establish the proposed capability. III. Capacity and Throughput Maximum number of F/A-18E/F and/or EA-18G aircraft the company could induct and complete annually. Expected induction ramp-up profile by year. Estimated average turnaround time from induction through return to the Fleet. Constraints that may limit throughput, including workforce, facilities, supply chain, engineering support, tooling, or Government-furnished material. Ability to adjust capacity in response to changing Fleet requirements or surge demand. Availability of funds to purchase all material to protect quantity throughput and maintain a stock of consumables to perform repair incidents throughout the modification (such as addressing corrosion), parts managements to include obsolescence and manufacturing parts capability. IV. Technical Capability Experience with F/A-18-series aircraft or comparable military tactical aircraft. Capability to perform structural inspections, repairs, modifications, TD incorporation, Non-destructive Inspections (NDI), wiring/electrical work, and systems troubleshooting. Capability to manufacture repair parts or develop repair procedures when required, using Government- or original equipment manufacturer-provided engineering direction. Ability to manage material procurement, kit installation, consumables, and repair-incident-to-modification requirements. Experience coordinating with the Defense Contract Management Agency (DCMA) or similar Government quality-assurance organizations. Ability to recruit, retain, and sustain sufficient qualified personnel to support anticipated SLM workload, including structural engineering personnel eligible for appointment as Naval Air Systems Command Designated Engineering Representatives (NAVDERs) to support the engineering analysis and disposition of aircraft-specific structural findings within the scope of authority delegated by NAVAIR. Respondents should describe their current and projected staffing capacity; recruitment, retention, and succession approaches; and ability to surge personnel as workload requires. V. Cybersecurity Ability to comply with applicable Department of the Navy, NAVAIR, and Department of War cybersecurity requirements for the protection, handling, storage, transmission, and access of Government information and data in performance of the proposed work. VI. Additional Information Identify any Government support, data, tooling, facilities, training, technical assistance, or other enablers that would be needed to establish or expand SLM capability. Provide any recommended acquisition, phasing, or transition approach that would help establish supplemental capacity while minimizing risk to Fleet readiness. 3. Response Instructions Responses should be limited to ten (10) pages and submitted electronically to jacob.r.heintze.civ@us.navy.mil no later than 3 December 2026. This RFI is issued for market research and planning purposes only. It is not a solicitation, request for proposal, or commitment by the Government to award a contract or reimburse any costs associated with responding. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation/notice; further written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation Number N6278927Q0001 is issued as a Request for Quotes (RFQ). The solicitation and incorporated provisions and clauses are in effect through the most current Federal Acquisition Circular (FAC) 2026-01 with an effective date of 13 March 2026. The Product and Service Code (PSC) is J019. The North American Industry Classification (NAICS) code is 336419. Supervisor of Shipbuilding Conversion and Repair, Groton CT (SSGR) intends to enter into a multiple award Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA), for a period of 5 years. The vendor shall refurbish weapon Shipping Harnesses in accordance with the attached specification. The Period of Performance shall be 27 January 2027 to 26 January 2032. Each BPA will have up to a five (5) year ordering period with a ceiling of up to $500,000. The BPA Call Limit will be $100,000. The ceiling of each agreement can be increased or decreased at any time by the Contracting Officer via bilateral modification to meet current and future requirements. Funding is not assigned to the BPA. The Government will only be obligated to the extent of calls placed against an awarded BPA. Each BPA call will be competed among the agreement holders as requirements arise. A call will then be placed based on the quote that is most advantageous to the Government. Offerors must provide a description of their property management system per FAR 45.201(c)(4) or confirmation of a property management system that has been reviewed and approved per DFARS 242.302 and meets the requirements of FAR 52.245-1(f). Offerors shall submit a pricing schedule that covers each year of the Period of Performance as follows: Fiscal Year Service Unit Unit Price Amount 2027 U-SSN 688 Weapon Shipping Harness Refurb 1 JOB $XX.XX $XX.XX 2028 U-SSN 688 Weapon Shipping Harness Refurb 1 JOB $XX.XX $XX.XX 2029 U-SSN 688 Weapon Shipping Harness Refurb 1 JOB $XX.XX $XX.XX 2030 U-SSN 688 Weapon Shipping Harness Refurb 1 JOB $XX.XX $XX.XX 2031 U-SSN 688 Weapon Shipping Harness Refurb 1 JOB $XX.XX $XX.XX Quotations are due prior to 4:00PM EST, 3 December 2026. Late submissions will not be accepted. Offers should be submitted via electronic commerce. The electronic address for receipt of offers is: kyle.r.berg3.civ@us.navy.mil and stephanie.l.neale.civ@us.navy.mil. Offerors should identify the RFQ number in the Subject Line of the email. Offerors are advised to submit electronic documents early and confirm successful transmission/receipt. The System for Award Management (SAM) is a Government maintained database of companies wanting to do business with the Government. A firm must register and maintain an active SAM registration in order to receive a federal award. Register at: https://sam.gov/SAM/pages/public/index.js EVALUATION FACTORS FOR AWARD: The Government intends to enter into a multiple award Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA), for a period of 5 years. Each BPA call will be competed among the agreement holders as requirements arise. The Government will make award(s) to the offeror(s) that represent the best value to the Government based on the following factors, in order: -Technical Qualifications/Ability to meet schedule -Past Performance -Price The Government intends to evaluate proposals and award a contract without discussions with offerors. However, the Government reserves the right to conduct discussions if later determined by the Contracting Officer to be necessary. The Government reserves the right to award one line, all line items, or any combination thereof. If multiple line items are awarded, cost/prices for each line item will be totaled and the award amount will be based on that total. See Section M of the solicitation for additional details.
